### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-non-gpu` · commit `7ba54ec6`

**TL;DR:** Two of the six build variants failed because meson could not fetch the `taskflow` subproject (`git clone https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow.git` → *"could not read Username for 'https://github.com'"*), and the two Test CPP failures are the same problem wearing a different mask — the `prometheus-cpp` wrap-git subproject is `required: false`, so it silently didn't build and all 15 `prometheusTelemetryTest` cases failed. Fix: fetch these two subprojects via `wrap-file` tarballs (or pre-seed them in the CI images) and gate the prometheus gtest sources on plugin availability.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** `nixl-ci-non-gpu` #3147: Build stages 438 (x86_64) and 400 (aarch64) failed at `meson setup` on the taskflow subproject git clone; Test CPP stages 485/498 failed with 15 `prometheusTelemetryTest` failures because `libtelemetry_exporter_prometheus.so` was never built.

**Root cause:** Both symptoms come from git-based meson subprojects being unfetchable in these CI containers. In stage 438/400:
```
Run-time dependency taskflow found: NO (tried pkgconfig and cmake)
Cloning into 'taskflow'...
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address
meson.build:233:16: ERROR: Git command failed: [... 'clone', '--depth','1','--branch','v3.10.0','https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow.git' ...]
```
Note that in the same log the `liburing` **wrap-file** tarball downloaded successfully — so plain HTTPS egress works, but `git clone` against github.com is answered with an auth challenge and git then prompts for credentials (no terminal → hard fail). The four variants whose Build stage passed had taskflow satisfied some other way, so this is image/environment-dependent, not commit-dependent.

The same unfetchable-wrap-git condition explains the Test CPP failures. `subprojects/prometheus-cpp.wrap` is also `[wrap-git]`, and the plugin is built only `if prometheus_sub.found()` with `required: false`, so the clone failure degrades to a warning and the plugin is skipped:
```
W nixl_plugin_manager.cpp:551 Plugin file does not exist: .../libtelemetry_exporter_prometheus.so
../test/gtest/telemetry_prometheus_test.cpp:157: Failure Expected: (handle) != (nullptr)
C++ exception "Failed to load telemetry plugin: prometheus"
FAILED TESTS (15/224): prometheusTelemetryTest.*
```
But `telemetry_prometheus_test.cpp` / `telemetry_histogram_test.cpp` are added to `gtest_sources` unconditionally, unlike the `telemetry_mp_*` tests which are guarded by `is_variable(...)` — so an optional, unavailable dependency turns into 15 hard test failures. The triggering commit (7ba54ec, a docs-only branch deprecating POSIX AIO) is unrelated; the `nixl_posix_aio_test` error lines in the log are expected negative-path output and the binary exits 0.

**Implicated commit:** 76275cfc "Use tagged Taskflow git wrap for NIXL builds (#2121)" — bzsuni (introduced the `[wrap-git]` taskflow fetch); not the build's trigger commit 7ba54ec.

**File:** `subprojects/taskflow.wrap:1-4` and `subprojects/prometheus-cpp.wrap:1-6`; consumers at `meson.build:233`, `src/plugins/telemetry/prometheus/meson.build:36`, `test/gtest/meson.build:112-115`

**Suggested fix:**
1. Convert both wraps from `[wrap-git]` to `[wrap-file]` release tarballs with `source_hash` (e.g. `https://github.com/taskflow/taskflow/archive/refs/tags/v3.10.0.tar.gz`), matching `liburing.wrap`, which demonstrably downloads fine in these containers. For prometheus-cpp keep `method = cmake` and inline the `fix-civetweb-security.patch` as `diff_files`.
2. Alternatively/additionally, pre-seed `subprojects/packagecache` (or install taskflow + prometheus-cpp) in the `nixl-ci-non-gpu-base-*` images so no network fetch happens at `meson setup`, and set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` in the CI env so a blocked clone fails with a clear error instead of a credential prompt.
3. Guard the prometheus test sources the same way the mp tests are: only add `telemetry_prometheus_test.cpp`, `telemetry_histogram_test.cpp`, `telemetry_prometheus_stress_test.cpp` when the prometheus exporter plugin was actually built (export a variable from `src/plugins/telemetry/prometheus/meson.build` and `is_variable()`-check it), or promote the subproject to `required: true` so a missing dependency fails loudly at configure time rather than as 15 opaque test failures.

**Related:** #2121 (introduced the taskflow git wrap). No existing issue found for the prometheus test gating — worth filing.

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` · commit `7ba54ec6`

**TL;DR:** All parallel container builds died at the same Dockerfile step — `git clone --recurse-submodules ... github.com/grpc/grpc` — with `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address`, i.e. GitHub returned 401/throttled the anonymous clones (4 concurrent builds × grpc's 16 submodules). Unrelated to this docs-only PR; make the gRPC clone resilient (retry loop, and stop recursing into submodules that aren't used).

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` #756: 3 of 4 parallel "Build image" stages failed at Dockerfile STEP 14/53 (gRPC build) because anonymous `git clone` from github.com was refused.

**Root cause:** Transient GitHub anonymous-access refusal / rate-limiting against the CI egress, not a code defect:

- Stage 207 (`node_id 207`, 11:36:11Z): top-level clone failed outright —
  `Cloning into 'grpc'... fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address` → `subprocess exited with status 128` → `Error: building at STEP "RUN git clone --recurse-submodules -b ${GRPC_TAG} ..."`.
- Stage 233 (11:35:50–11:36:02Z): top-level clone succeeded, then 13 of 16 submodules failed with the identical message (`benchmark`, `bloaty`, `boringssl`, `cares`, `envoy-api`, `googleapis`, `googletest`, `opentelemetry`, `protobuf`, `protoc-gen-validate`, `re2`, `xds`, `zlib`). Retry recovered some (`benchmark`), but `Failed to clone 'third_party/bloaty' a second time, aborting` → exit status 1.
- The partial/mixed pattern is the tell: `abseil-cpp` cloned fine seconds earlier in both stages, and some grpc submodules succeeded while neighbours failed at the same instant. `could not read Username ... No such device or address` is git being handed an HTTP 401 and having no tty to prompt on — GitHub's response when it throttles unauthenticated clones. Four container variants building in parallel, each recursively cloning 16 grpc submodules, is enough to trip that.

There is no hang: timestamps are continuous, failure to error is ~20 s. The PR is `docs/deprecate-posix-aio` (documentation) and touches nothing in the build; no recent commit touches the gRPC step (last Dockerfile changes: d2495941, [REDACTED:Hex High Entropy String], e6fb7714 — torch index, base images, cuObject).

**Implicated commit:** none — infrastructure/network, not a code regression (the failing step predates the recent Dockerfile commits)

**File:** contrib/Dockerfile:178 (and the same pattern at :161, :201, :208, :213)

**Suggested fix:**
1. Immediate: re-run the build — this class of failure is transient.
2. Stop recursing into submodules that aren't used. The cmake invocation sets `gRPC_SSL_PROVIDER=package`, `gRPC_ABSL_PROVIDER=package`, `gRPC_ZLIB_PROVIDER=package`, so only `third_party/protobuf` (and its deps) is needed as `module`. Replace the blanket `--recurse-submodules` with a shallow clone plus targeted `git submodule update --init --depth 1 third_party/protobuf`, which removes ~14 clones per build — including `bloaty`, `benchmark` and `googletest`, which are test/tooling-only and are what actually aborted the build.
3. Wrap each `git clone`/`submodule update` in a retry-with-backoff helper (git has no equivalent of the `wget --tries=3 --waitretry=5` already used for the DOCA deb on line 135), and add `-c protocol.version=2 -c credential.helper= -c core.askPass=true` / `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` so a 401 fails fast and loudly instead of appearing as a credential-prompt error.
4. Longer term: pre-bake abseil/gRPC into the CI base image or mirror them internally (as was done for apt via `APT_MIRROR`), so per-PR builds don't hit github.com N times in parallel.

**Related:** none found — issue search for this error signature returned no matching reports.

</details>

### svc-nixl · 2026-09-23

🤖 **CI Triage Agent** — `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` · commit `7ba54ec6`

**TL;DR:** Two of the four parallel container builds died on unauthenticated `git clone` from github.com — `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address` — i.e. GitHub refused anonymous access (rate limit/auth challenge) and git had no tty to prompt on; the fix is to authenticate (or mirror/cache) the third-party clones, as PR #2263 already proposes.

<details><summary>Full analysis</summary>

**Summary:** `nixl-ci-build-container-pr` #768 failed in two of four parallel "Build image" stages (node 198 x86_64, node 205 aarch64) when a Dockerfile `RUN git clone` step against github.com failed with exit status 128.

**Root cause:** Not a code defect and unrelated to this PR's docs-only change. Both stages fail identically on anonymous HTTPS clones from github.com:

- Stage 198 (x86_64), STEP 20/53 — `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-cpp.git`:
  `Cloning into 'azure-sdk-for-cpp'... fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address` → `subprocess exited with status 128`
- Stage 205 (aarch64), STEP 18/53 — `git clone --recurse-submodules ... https://github.com/aws/aws-sdk-cpp.git --branch 1.11.760`: the top-level repo and 12 of 13 submodules cloned fine, then `Unable to fetch in submodule path 'crt/aws-crt-cpp/crt/s2n'` with the same "could not read Username" error, then `Failed to recurse into submodule path 'crt/aws-crt-cpp'` → exit 128.

GitHub returns an auth challenge (401/429) rather than serving the repo when anonymous request limits are exceeded; git then tries to prompt for a username, and in a non-interactive build there is no tty, producing exactly this message. The transient/throttling nature is evidenced within the same build: stages 233 and 187 completed those identical clone steps successfully, and in the failing aarch64 stage the immediately preceding `etcd-cpp-apiv3` clone and the aws-sdk-cpp top-level clone both succeeded — only one submodule fetch was rejected. Four architecture variants building in parallel, each doing dozens of clones (grpc + submodules, aws-sdk-cpp + 13 submodules, abseil, azure, gusli, ucx), all from one CI egress IP, is enough to trip the anonymous limit. No timestamp gaps or hangs: the failures are immediate, ~1 s after the clone starts.

**Implicated commit:** unknown — no commit introduced this; the failing clone steps are long-standing (`contrib/Dockerfile` last touched by d2495941, NirWolfer, unrelated to these lines).

**File:** `contrib/Dockerfile:208` (aws-sdk-cpp, aarch64 stage) and `contrib/Dockerfile:218` (azure-sdk-for-cpp, x86_64 stage)

**Suggested fix:**
1. Land/adopt PR #2263 ("ci: authenticate third-party github.com clones") so these fetches use a token instead of anonymous access — authenticated requests get a far higher rate limit and never fall back to a credential prompt. Pass the credential via a BuildKit secret or `git config --global url."https://<token>@github.com/".insteadOf`, never as a build ARG that lands in an image layer.
2. Regardless of auth, make these steps non-interactive and self-retrying so a throttled response fails loudly instead of hanging on a prompt: set `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and wrap each clone in a retry loop (3 attempts, backoff), matching the `wget --tries=3 --waitretry=5` pattern already used for libfabric/DOCA/rustup in the same Dockerfile.
3. Longer term, pull these pinned third-party sources from an internal mirror/artifact cache (as was done for apt in #1961) so container builds don't depend on github.com availability at all.
4. Retrigger build #768 — it will likely pass on its own.

**Related:** https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2263 (ci: authenticate third-party github.com clones) — directly addresses this failure mode; https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/1961 (precedent for mirroring external dependencies).

</details>
